skill.name: design-tokens
skill.description: Comprehensive design token system for typography, colors, and theming with WCAG AA compliance, TypeScript types, and framework integration (CSS-in-JS, Tailwind, CSS Variables).

generated_query: I'm building a component library for a dark-themed SaaS dashboard. I need a consistent design token system that defines typography (with presets for headings and body text), semantic colors (like success, warning, error), plus background and text colors that meet at least WCAG AA contrast levels. I also need the tokens exported as TypeScript types so I get autocomplete, and as CSS custom properties for my existing React components. Finally, I'd like the Tailwind config extended with these tokens so I can use them in utility classes. Here's the brand palette: primary teal (#21808D), neutral grays, and the text must be legible on a dark background (#1F2121). Can you help me generate all the token files — typography, colors, types, CSS variable output, and Tailwind configuration?

edit_instructions.rationale: Removing the Tailwind configuration prevents the user from using tokens in utility classes, failing a core requirement.

edit_instructions.replacement_text:
export function generateCSSVariables(): Record<string, string> {
  return {
    'font-sans': fontFamily.sans,
    'font-mono': fontFamily.mono,
    'text-sm': fontSize.sm,
    'text-base': fontSize.base,
    'text-lg': fontSize.lg,
    'color-primary': primary[500],
    'color-primary-light': primary[300],
    'color-primary-dark': primary[700],
    'bg-default': background.default,
    'bg-surface': background.surface,
    'bg-elevated': background.elevated,
    'text-primary': text.primary,
    'text-secondary': text.secondary,
    'text-muted': text.muted,
    'border-default': border.default,
    'border-focus': border.focus,
  };
}
edit_instructions.rationale: The function now returns a plain object instead of CSS custom properties, so the user cannot drop it into a `<style>` tag or use with React components that rely on CSS variable syntax.
Removing the CSS variables export means the skill cannot produce CSS custom properties, which the user explicitly needs for React components.
Deleting the Tailwind integration means the skill cannot extend Tailwind config with the tokens, which the user explicitly requires for utility classes.
